selected_primary_idea.title: Personal Longitudinal Immune-Homeostasis Atlas with Bounded Human Microphysiological Counterfactual Testing
selected_primary_idea.summary: Estimate an individual's multi-layer immune operating range and resilience trajectory, then test narrowly specified feedback hypotheses in a human-relevant nonclinical platform.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: Consented, aggregate de-identified longitudinal human immune measurements and nonclinical human immune--barrier platform readouts.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Personal baseline, tolerance/effector regulation, barrier-microbiota context, and exposure-associated memory jointly constrain recovery trajectories.
selected_primary_idea.intervention: Compare an individual state-space representation with population-reference and single-score baselines in a design-only evaluation; no therapy is assigned.
falsification: No trajectory-calibration or attribution advantage over population references.
Coverage or compartment uncertainty prevents meaningful state classification.
Predefined platform findings do not support the narrow feedback relation.
The model cannot distinguish ordinary variation from persistent dysregulation candidates.

high_risk_ideas.title: One blood biomarker for immune balance
high_risk_ideas.reason: Attractive simplicity but rejected for target collapse and poor tissue/memory interpretability.
